- **Pulleys, block and tackle, treadwheel crane** [`block_and_tackle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/block_and_tackle.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Brunelleschi's reversible hoist and cranes for the dome are remembered and copied into engineers' notebooks. Local: Opera del Duomo; Giuliano da Sangallo; Bonaccorso Ghiberti.
- **Wheelbarrow** [`wheelbarrow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wheelbarrow.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Archimedes' screw (water screw)** [`archimedes_screw`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/archimedes_screw.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept high. Revived on paper by Taccola and Francesco di Giorgio; actual drainage and irrigation mostly use bucket wheels and chains of pots. Local: Francesco di Giorgio Martini (Siena); coopers and carpenters.
- **Gears and gear trains** [`gears_gear_trains`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gears_gear_trains.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Mills use wooden peg wheels and lantern pinions; clockmakers file brass and iron wheels by hand. Nobody has a theory of tooth shape. Local: millwrights; Lorenzo della Volpaia.
- **Cam and camshaft** [`cam_camshaft`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cam_camshaft.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: fulling mills on the Arno; paper mills at Colle di Val d'Elsa.
- **Screw, nut and bolt** [`screw_nut_bolt`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/screw_nut_bolt.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Big wooden screws work oil, wine, cloth and printing presses. Metal screws are filed by hand for armour and clocks; no nut fits another maker's bolt. Local: press makers; armourers; clockmakers.
- **Belt, rope and chain drives** [`belt_drive`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/belt_drive.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Cord bands drive spinning wheels, lathes and gem cutters' wheels. Flat leather belts on shafting and link chains for power are unknown.
- **Ball and roller bearings** [`ball_bearings`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ball_bearings.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Axles run in greased wood, bronze or iron. Wooden rollers are easy; hard, truly round metal balls of equal size are not.
- **Bellows and the double-acting piston blower** [`bellows_piston_blower`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bellows_piston_blower.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Leather bellows, water-driven at ironworks, are standard. The wooden double-acting piston box that blows on both strokes is unknown. Local: ironworks of the Tuscan coast and Pistoia hills; bronze founders. Elsewhere: China, double-acting box bellows.
- **Water-powered trip hammer and stamp mill** [`trip_hammer_water_powered`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trip_hammer_water_powered.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: Gualchiere di Remole (the wool guild's fulling mills on the Arno); iron hammer mills (magli); paper mills at Colle di Val d'Elsa.
- **Lost-wax casting** [`lost_wax_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lost_wax_casting.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Florence leads Europe in bronze casting; Verrocchio died in 1488, his workshop tradition is alive. Local: Bertoldo di Giovanni (Medici sculpture garden; dies 1491); bronze founders and goldsmiths. Elsewhere: Milan, Leonardo's giant Sforza horse project.
- **Sand and loam moulding for large castings** [`sand_loam_casting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sand_loam_casting.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Bells and cannon are cast in loam moulds built for one pour. Reusable flasks of damp sand and thin-walled cast-iron pots are unknown. Local: bell founders; cannon founders; Bonaccorso Ghiberti.
- **Wire drawing** [`wire_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wire_drawing.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Goldsmiths draw gold and silver wire for brocade thread through drawplates by hand. Iron wire comes from Lombardy and Nuremberg. Local: goldsmiths; gold thread makers of the silk guild. Elsewhere: Nuremberg, water-powered wire mills.
- **Rolling and slitting mill** [`rolling_mill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/rolling_mill.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Sheet metal and coin blanks are hammered. Small rolls for gold, lead or tin are makeable; true cylindrical rolls and a stiff frame are the difficulty. Local: the Zecca (mint); goldsmiths; goldbeaters.
- **Precision cylinder boring** [`boring_machine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boring_machine.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Bronze guns are cast around a core and at best reamed smooth. A rigid, guided boring bar that makes a true cylinder is new. Local: bronze founders; cannon founders; Leonardo da Vinci (in Milan).
- **Screw-cutting lathe with slide rest** [`lathe_screw_cutting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lathe_screw_cutting.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept high. Turners use pole and bow lathes that spin back and forth, tool held by hand. A lead screw with tool slide is drawn in one south German manuscript. Local: wood turners; clockmakers; pewterers. Elsewhere: Upper Rhine and Nuremberg (the Housebook's screw-cutting lathe).
- **Precision measurement (flat surfaces, gauges, micrometer)** [`precision_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/precision_measurement.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Parts are fitted to each other by eye, dividers and callipers. Every city has its own braccio; there are no gauges or flat reference plates.
- **Machine tools (planer, shaper, milling machine)** [`machine_tools`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/machine_tools.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium
- **Interchangeable parts** [`interchangeable_parts`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interchangeable_parts.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Cast printing type demonstrates the value of common dimensions. Armourers and clockmakers still fit most components individually. Local: type founders and printers. Elsewhere: Venice Arsenal, standardisation of galley components.
- **Assembly line and mass production** [`assembly_line`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/assembly_line.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. The wool trade already splits work into dozens of steps, but spread across homes and shops. Guild statutes fix who may do what. Local: Arte della Lana; Arte della Seta. Elsewhere: Venice Arsenal, organised stages of ship construction and fitting out.
- **Water-powered sawmill** [`sawmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sawmill.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept medium. Camaldoli's accounts record a water saw in 1442. Casentino timber also travels down the Arno by raft. A millwright can inspect an operating local precedent. Local: Camaldoli sawmill in the Casentino; Opera del Duomo forests. Elsewhere: Venetian Alps and southern Germany, water-powered sawmills.
- **Spinning wheel** [`spinning_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_wheel.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Country women spin for the wool guild; the distaff is still preferred for strong warp yarn. The flyer that spins and winds at once is brand new in Germany. Local: lanaioli (wool merchants) and their spinners in the contado. Elsewhere: Southern Germany, drawings of flyer-and-bobbin spinning wheels (c. 1480).
- **Spinning machines (jenny, water frame, mule)** [`spinning_machines`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spinning_machines.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept low. Silk is twisted on big circular throwing mills with hundreds of spindles. Nothing similar exists for wool or cotton, whose spinning feeds thousands of households. Local: Florentine silk throwsters (hand-turned mills); Arte della Seta. Elsewhere: Bologna, water-driven silk mills (a guarded secret); Lucca.
- **Horizontal treadle loom** [`treadle_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/treadle_loom.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: wool weavers; silk drawloom weavers.
- **Flying shuttle and power loom** [`power_loom`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/power_loom.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. A flying shuttle is carpenter's work; a powered loom is far harder. Weavers are poor dependants of the guild merchants and fear for their bread (Ciompi revolt, 1378).
- **Cotton gin** [`cotton_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cotton_gin.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Cotton arrives already cleaned, in bales from Syria and Cyprus via Venice, for Lombard fustian. No one in Tuscany handles seed cotton. Elsewhere: India and the Levant, roller gins.
- **Stocking frame (knitting machine)** [`knitting_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/knitting_frame.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Hose are cut and sewn from woven cloth; hand knitting on needles is known. A frame needs hundreds of identical fine sprung hooks.
